correctness.rationale: For every T>0, u,v,w>0 with u+v+w<=1 and nonnegative gap fractions summing to one, an actual operating configuration has random-arrival mean wait equal to the sum of squared realized cyclic gaps divided by 2T. Taking the four-mode expectation yields the exact stated quadratic. Symmetrization c=d strictly lowers the objective unless already equal; w>0 guarantees strict convexity on the entire feasible simplex. Solving the reduced stationary equations gives positive a,c,d and a possibly negative b. The sign of b is precisely the sign of w(u+v+w)-uv. When it is negative, setting b=0 yields a positive boundary point with zero tangent derivative and interior one-sided derivative 2[uv-w(u+v+w)]/(4u+3v+3w)>0. Convex KKT conditions establish global uniqueness. Substitution yields the radical transition and rational benchmark. Standard-library exact-rational checker independently evaluates 165 positive rational parameter triples and candidate schedules; no finite test is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Completed statement-level comparison distinguishes the result from earlier independent-cancellation timetables (which require independent service operation) and earlier correlated schedules with only two optional departures. In the accessible full-text bus-planning papers, operations are modeled through stochastic travel time, vehicle capacity or transfer coordination; neither contains the specified joint operating-pattern law, explicit uv=w(u+v+w) activation boundary, or proof of a positive-cooccurrence co-dispatch region. Targeted literature and mathematical-record searches did not identify a theorem that implies the complete result. This is an informed but non-independent priority assessment, subject to the recorded residual risk.
residual_risks: Full text of Zhao et al. (2006) and the specific 2019 rolling-rescheduling paper was not inspected; the latter has an indexed headway-squared objective but no demonstrated equivalent boundary.
Classical robust timetabling, stochastic service planning or quadratic scenario-optimization treatments may imply this specific low-dimensional boundary without stating it in the same form.
The classification fixes a particular three-mode support of the jointly operating candidates and does not characterize all possible correlated service laws.

value.rationale: The nonlinear-looking policy decision of whether to bunch or spread service is governed by an exact and nontrivial correlation-dependent algebraic threshold, with positive all-service probability on both sides. The fully classified three-parameter operating law corresponds to alternation between one optional vehicle, a pair of other optional vehicles, and a simultaneous full-service contingency. At equal partial-mode weights the natural phase boundary is 3-2sqrt(2), and a rational benchmark produces 11.5179% lower expected waiting time than uniform nominal departures. Unlike a routine reparameterization, the finding makes clear when full nominal frequency should be deliberately reduced by co-dispatch even though every candidate is sometimes present, with an exact unique optimizer and sensitivity boundary. Its value is as a transparent mathematical benchmark, not a field recommendation.
